chunks: Say: "Whether you conceal or reveal whatsoever is in your hearts it is all known to God, as is known to Him all that is in the heavens and the earth; and God has the power over all things."
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God's knowledge of what is in our hearts?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to validate the concept of 'Ilm al-Ghayb' (Knowledge of the Unseen) as a divine attribute shared by the Prophet and the Imams, who possess knowledge of what is in the hearts. It underscores the spiritual reality that outward actions are merely reflections of inner states, a theme central to the Shia emphasis on sincerity (Ikhlas) and the infallible guidance of the Ahl al-Bayt. The verse concludes by affirming God's absolute power, linking His comprehensive knowledge with His ability to enact judgment.
